title: Four advantages MacBook Pro redesign will have over current model
snippet: Next week Apple will unveil its first MacBook Pro redesign in five years. Rumors indicate the new MacBook Pro will have the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as current models, but with exclusive advantages in at least four other areas. more…
fullText:
Next week Apple will unveil its first MacBook Pro redesign in five years. Rumors indicate the new MacBook Pro will have the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as current models, but with exclusive advantages in at least four other areas.

#1: Significantly lighter industrial design

While the new MacBook Pro design is expected to be a little thinner than the current model, its biggest design advantage is a weight reduction. Per Mark Gurman:

The new MacBook Pros are lighter — significantly lighter. Apple has reengineered the machine’s interior miniaturizing parts and rearranging components to make the computer much easier to carry.

If you’re worried about Apple removing ports with its MacBook Pro redesign, it sounds like the company probably learned its lesson from previous generations. Since the design isn’t expected to slim down too much, it’s likely there will be minimal changes to ports.

#2: OLED display

The Liquid Retina XDR display on current MacBook Pros is an excellent display. But Apple plans to make its new MacBook Pro display even better by introducing OLED.

OLED has been used in iPhones for years, but the only example of Apple using it on larger displays is the iPad Pro. The tandem OLED introduced on iPad in 2024 was touted by Apple as “the world’s most advanced display.”

Now, OLED is coming to the Mac with the new MacBook Pro. And if it’s anything like what the iPad Pro offers, the new display is bound to impress.

#3: Touch support

Most MacBook Pro users probably aren’t asking for touch support. But if you’re like me, you may find that there are some cases where it would be valuable if you could touch the Mac’s display.

Apple’s new MacBook Pro will make that possible. Its OLED display will include full touchscreen capabilities and benefit from touch optimizations throughout macOS Golden Gate.

Touch isn’t replacing the primary input methods of trackpad and keyboard. Rather, it’s being introduced as a secondary “nice-to-have” option.

#4: Notch-free display

Apple’s last MacBook Pro redesign in 2021 brought the notch to the Mac. And this redesign will reportedly remove it.

	

Like Apple has done on the iPhone, it’s removing the notch first on its Pro line. The new MacBook Pro drops the notch, reportedly in favor of a hole-punch camera cutout.

A new Dynamic Island feature is expected to be introduced too, though there’s a chance it might come to older Macs via a software update.

snippet: iOS 27.2 launches next week with a variety of new features, and also design changes for select Apple apps. Here’s what’s coming. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 launches next week with a variety of new features, and also design changes for select Apple apps. Here’s what’s coming.

#1: Apple Music

Apple Music just rolled out a big design rebrand, and iOS 27.2 extends that fresh visual identity to several aspects of the Music app.

For starters, there’s a new app icon that strips the old red color in favor of black and white. The removal of the old red identity extends to other elements inside the app too.

In Music’s tab bar, the accent color for the active tab is now blue instead of red. And in your Library, sections like Playlists, Artists, and Albums are entirely monochrome.

If you use the Music app’s widgets on your Home Screen or Today view, you’ll notice that they drop the former red background too. Now all widgets use a black background instead.

#2: Apple Books

Apple’s Books app in iOS 27.2 introduces design updates centered around its reading experience.

As explained in-depth here, design changes include:

Progress bars are now available to track your reading location

Menu in the bottom-right has a new icon and is a standard Liquid Glass menu for consistency with other apps

Bookmark has been removed from that menu and now lives in the upper-right of the reader view as a standalone button

‘X’ button has moved to the upper-left corner

‘Back’ button has moved to lower-left and is larger than before

These changes were likely motivated by the iPhone Duo’s introduction. 

Not only does the Duo make a great e-reader, but it’s also a reason to avoid bespoke UI elements for things like menus and buttons, since Apple’s stock options dynamically reposition for different iPhone models in a way the old Books controls likely wouldn’t have.

New Apple Books menu (left) and old (right)

title: Google upgrading Gemini for Android Auto with Personal Intelligence
snippet: Google is beginning to roll out Personal Intelligence for Gemini on Android Auto and Android Automotive (cars with Google built-in). more…
fullText:
Google is beginning to roll out Personal Intelligence for Gemini on Android Auto and Android Automotive (cars with Google built-in).

Like in the Gemini app or AI Mode, Personal Intelligence taps into your Google Workspace (including Gmail and Calendar), Photos, Maps, Search, and YouTube to personalize responses. Your prompts and commands don’t have to include specifics as Personal Intelligence can pull those details from emails, photos, or a “place you saved in Google Maps.”

This allows for complex or natural queries, like “What’s my flight gate? And is my flight on time?” or “Take me to my doctor’s appointment.”

“You don’t have to hunt for the confirmation email, then do a separate search for delays. Gemini gives you both answers in one go.”

“You don’t have to remember the street address or look it up before you drive.”

Additionally, Gemini is aware of your preferences when you say: “Find me an indoor restaurant along my route that matches my usual vibe.” This saves you from having to specify you’re vegetarian with every command.

	

Other examples include:

Retrieve details without pulling over: Trying to return to a place you saw earlier? Say, “Find the car wash from the photo I took last week and navigate there.” You don’t need to scroll through your camera roll or pull over to get the name and directions. 

Pick up where you left off: Heading out for the morning? Say, “Take me to the coffee shop we were talking about yesterday”. Gemini will handle the digging and send you on your way.

	

On the privacy front, Personal Intelligence is opt-in, though it will come to Android Auto automatically if you enabled it for the Gemini app on your phone.

If you don’t use Personal Intelligence, everything in the car still works: You can use navigation, listen to music, make calls, and ask questions, but the answers won’t be tailored to you.

Meanwhile, on Android Automotive, Personal Intelligence will only share personalized responses “when you’re in the car with your phone connected.” 

Personal Intelligence is rolling out starting today to Android Auto, with Android Automotive availability in the coming months.

title: Apple’s New iPad Mini Gets OLED and Water Resistance
snippet: On the heels of the Duo, here comes the Mini. It’s arriving Nov. 6.
fullText:
The new iPhone Duo, unfolded, almost feels like an iPad Mini. But if you want the real thing, Apple also has a new iPad Mini coming on Nov. 6. The upgrade, which starts at $699, adds a larger OLED screen and water resistance for the first time.

The new iPad Mini has been expected for months, and it was announced two days ahead of an expected showcase of new Macs on Wednesday. It has a number of updates this time around, making it look, on paper, like a killer upgrade for anyone who’s been waiting for one. Unfortunately, it’s also more expensive than before.

One of the two new iPad Mini colors, midnight.Apple

The $699 starting price comes with 128GB of storage, with 256 and 512GB options that are $799 and $999. Compared to the last iPad Mini, which came out two years ago, the new one has an A20 processor (upgraded from A17), but also has a larger display (8.5 inches compared to the older one’s 8.3) that’s also OLED for the first time. The front-facing camera’s also been shifted to the landscape edge, matching the other iPads and making it more centered for video chats if you’re standing it on a table in a case.

			

More from CNET

It’s thinner and lighter than before, but also is the first iPad that’s water-resistant (IP67), which means it could survive pool, ocean or tub dunks. There’s a through-screen speaker system on this model, too, which I’m curious to try. It’s called Acoustic Display.

The Mini’s available to order on Oct. 28, and is going on sale Nov. 6. We’ll have more thoughts when I eventually get to review one, but for anyone who’s wanted a new Mini and didn’t want to spring for a Duo this iPad looks like good news.

The other iPad Mini color, starlight.Apple

title: Galaxy S27 might drop to 8GB of RAM; other Android phones could go back to 4GB
snippet: As the AI industry continues to directly cause a crisis in the availability of RAM, new rumors suggest that the Galaxy S27 could downgrade to 8GB of RAM, while other Android brands could go back to 4GB for some models. more…
fullText:
As the AI industry continues to directly cause a crisis in the availability of RAM, new rumors suggest that the Galaxy S27 could downgrade to 8GB of RAM, while other Android brands could go back to 4GB for some models.

RAM allotments in modern smartphones are fairly predictable. 12GB or 16GB in a high-end flagship, at least 8GB in most mid-range devices, and around 6GB in most entry-level devices. 4GB isn’t uncommon in entry-level devices, but even the most affordable models have pushed to 6GB in recent years because, frankly, Android just doesn’t run all that well on 4GB anymore. 

But everyone is feeling the strain of the rapidly rising cost of memory. A recent report even claims that Samsung doesn’t make a profit when it sells a Galaxy device.

With that in mind, it’s not entirely surprising to hear that Samsung is considering a downgrade for its upcoming Galaxy S27 series. Leaker and analyst @kro_roe on Twitter/X says that the Galaxy S27 series will see its base models start with 8GB of RAM rather than the 12GB that’s been standard for the past two generations. Specifically, Galaxy S25 and Galaxy S26 both start with 12GB of RAM, with a 16GB option for select trims of the Ultra model.

	

This latest leak shows configurations with 8GB of RAM as the starting amount, and 12GB across the Pro and Ultra tiers.

Galaxy S27: 8GB/256GB, 12GB/512GB

Galaxy S27+: 8GB/256GB, 12GB/512GB

Galaxy S27 Pro: 12GB/256GB, 12GB/512GB, 16GB “under consideration”

Galaxy S27 Ultra: 12GB/256GB, 12GB/512GB, 16GB/1TB

	

The same leaker says the price increases “may be unavoidable” and that promos like doubled storage may not show up during the pre-order period. Meanwhile, the actual storage type could also differ, with some models “differentiating UFS storage versions” to balance costs. Galaxy S26 used UFS 4.0 across the board.

Samsung might not be alone in these downgrades. Another leaker on Weibo claims that “several” other Android brands are dropping their “top-of-the-line” devices to 12GB, their “main” mid-range models to 8GB, and entry-level devices to 6GB as the “top-of-the-line” offering, with most of those lower-cost Android phones going back to just 4GB of RAM.

It’s hard to know for certain what the future holds at this point, as “RAMageddon” rages on. All we know is that everything is getting more expensive. Thanks AI.

title: Apple says developers are showing ‘incredible’ support for the iPhone Duo
snippet: One of the major issues raised by early reviews of the iPhone Duo is limited support by third-party apps. As we noted in our own review, there are three tiers of support currently, the worst of which sees an iPhone app stranded in the center of a mostly black area of the display. The good news is that Apple says the position is changing rapidly, citing “incredible” support for the larger display of the folding iPhone … more…
fullText:
One of the major issues raised by early reviews of the iPhone Duo is limited support by third-party apps. As we noted in our own review, there are three tiers of support currently, the worst of which sees an iPhone app stranded in the center of a mostly black area of the display. 

The good news is that Apple says the position is changing rapidly, citing “incredible” support for the larger display of the folding iPhone …

Apple says developers are taking advantage of the flexibility of the iPhone Duo in order to create exciting new experiences.

With an inner display that’s 50 percent larger than iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the flexibility to use iPhone Duo in a variety of poses, developers are enhancing their apps to create exciting new experiences for capturing and sharing memories, streaming entertainment, gaming, multitasking, and much more […]

“The response to iPhone Duo from our developer community has been incredible, and we’re inspired by how quickly they’ve embraced its larger display and new ways to interact,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations. “From watching popular shows and content on the expansive inner display to multitasking across windows or playing console-quality games, developers around the world are reimagining what their apps can do. We can’t wait for users to discover these experiences beginning this Friday, with many more app experiences to follow.”

The company says it will be highlighting some of the best iPhone Duo apps and games on the App Store tomorrow when the new device goes on sale. Apple has already named some of them, starting with streaming video services.

 Netflix makes finding great entertainment even more fun: Members can scroll through Clips on the outer display and then open iPhone Duo to keep watching on the large nano-texture inner display, with Clips switching seamlessly between a vertical or horizontal view.

More streaming services — including Prime Video and Paramount+ — are joining Apple TV in using the larger canvas for movies and series. With iPhone Duo, Prime Video enhances the viewing experience for users as they stream premium entertainment, and when partially folded, content plays on the top half of the display while X-Ray details showing cast and bonus content appear on the bottom half. Paramount+ offers richer playback controls and expanded browsing for shows and live channels.

Two key sports apps have also been updated to take advantage of the new opportunities.

When iPhone Duo is propped open on a table, users can easily enjoy content hands-free, without a stand. Sports fans can follow MLBand PGA Tour with live games and highlights, plus real-time scores, stats, and leaderboards on the larger display.

“Baseball fans are incredibly passionate about the sport, and they follow our games as closely as they can. Now, iPhone Duo provides an exciting new fan engagement platform by showcasing the action and information simultaneously,” said Kenny Gersh, MLB’s executive vice president of Media, Business Development, and Product. “This incredible device unlocks a fun, versatile way to experience baseball from anywhere, and we’re grateful to have worked with Apple to ensure the app is ready for the World Series. Set iPhone Duo on a table partially folded and the live game plays on the upright half of the display while real-time stats fill the half resting on the table, so fans never have to choose between the broadcast and the box score.”

	

Apple says that Microsoft Word and Outlook will roll out a desktop-class experience in the next few weeks, while Zoom, Slack, and Salesforce are also prepping their own updates.

Zoom turns the inner display into an immersive video conference room, so users can see shared content and other participants at the same time. Slack brings a user’s whole workspace into view, making it easy to follow channels and automate tasks. Salesforce helps teams manage customer relationships and act on business insights, with more of their dashboards in view.

The company goes on to name other apps, including Fantastical, Notewise, Things, Bear, Detail, Instagram, Edits, and VLLO. Apple Arcade games ready for the new form factor include Sneaky Sasquatch and Retrocade.

More apps and sample screenshots are shared in the company’s announcement.

If you’ve already ordered the iPhone Duo or are heading to an Apple store to try one, reviewers recommend trying the inner display in both landscape and portrait modes to see which delivers the better experience. Different third-party apps tend to be optimized for one or the other.

title: Wyze Solar Cam has a 2K camera and needs just an hour of sunlight to keep recording
snippet: Wyze is launching a new Solar Cam that has a camera that matches the best Google Nest has to offer, while needing just an hour of sunlight to avoid needing to manually recharge. more…
fullText:
Wyze is launching a new Solar Cam that has a camera that matches the best Google Nest has to offer, while needing just an hour of sunlight to avoid needing to manually recharge.

Wyze has a camera for basically every need, and its latest is one that works outdoors with potentially limitless battery life. The Wyze Solar Cam bundles a 2K camera with a 1.77W solar panel that Wyze says needs just an hour of direct sunlight to keep charged.

The camera houses a 5,200 mAh battery to ensure it can run in the case of crummy weather or having its solar panel blocked, but in direct sunlight, the panel doesn’t need much to maintain the battery. That’s nothing super new – Wyze itself launched a Solar Cam Pan with the same promise last year, and plenty of other brands have done the same. You can even add a solar panel to a Nest Cam if you really want to.

The benefit of this latest Wyze Solar Cam comes partially in the resolution, with a 2304 x 1296 2K camera that features 130-degree field of view and color night vision. It also has a 100 lumen spotlight built-in and optional local microSD card recording. 

	

Wyze Solar Cam is available today for $69.98, with the camera also available without the solar panel for $10 less.

fullText:
Good morning. Today I’m reading about an incredible medical plagiarism scandal, replaying the original Ocarina of Time ahead of its remake’s November 5th release, jamming to the dark new Fontaines D.C. album, and using Gemini to prep for the upcoming fantasy basketball season.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

Over the course of Friday, it quickly became clear that demand for the iPhone Duo far outstripped initial supply. Apple’s first foldable went on sale at 8am on the 16th, and delivery dates immediately got pushed back to November, then December, and now January. Analysts had warned that Apple wouldn’t be able to keep pace with interest, despite the phone’s $2,000 price, but the company called it “nothing short of extraordinary” in a statement released to the media.

	

Samsung was benefiting before Apple even opened the order books. Its UK mobile leadership says purchases of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 family are up 16% since launch, while Google searches for Samsung foldables rose 300% over the preceding month.

The big question, though, is whether the Duo’s existence will bring the book-style foldable — and by extension, the $2,000 smartphone — into the mainstream. Samsung has been beating this drum since 2019, but foldable share still sits at a mere 2% of the overall smartphone market, and most units sold are the smaller, cheaper flip-style variety. The Duo is expected to give Apple a 25% share of the entire foldable market by the end of 2026, which should broaden acceptance of the form factor across the industry.

I’m not surprised by the uptick in interest; the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is undoubtedly my favorite foldable ever, owing to its novel and pocketable design. I’ve always enjoyed reading on book-style foldables, but with the Fold 8 I often forget I’m using a phone entirely.

Will there be a day when, say,  a decade from now, foldables are the conventional smartphone choice and slab phones of any kind are considered budget alternatives? In a world where component prices stay elevated and companies continue to pad their margins with premium options at the expense of the entry class, that’s a real possibility. Either way, the Duo validates far more than Samsung’s decision to experiment with foldables all those years ago; its unprecedented demand hints at a sea change in how people want to use their phones, and the compromises they’re willing to accept in order to get there.

iPhone Duo orders are delayed into 2027; here are the Android foldables you should try instead

iPhone Duo has a bigger battery than Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Pixel 11 Pro Fold

✉️ Inbox

The biggest reason not to buy a Googlebook is all about timing. Ben’s Weekender essay focuses on how the Googlebook OS fiasco is exacerbated by the fact that every Googlebook laptop is like $300 too expensive.

HP Googlebook 14 review: Great laptop, shame about the OS. 😬

XREAL 1 Pro+ has exactly the right hardware upgrades at the same $599 price. If the $1,279 XREAL wants for the Aura feels steep, this entertainment-focused option is a perfect alternative.

Google rolling out Universal Cart that lets you shop the web and find deals with Gemini, Search. I suspect we will look back on the introduction of Universal Cart as the beginning of the end of traditional Google Search.

Google’s Universal Cart puts a shopping cart everywhere, including Search homepage, Chrome

YouTube reportedly ‘looking’ into adding audiobooks to Premium. Competition in the market? We love to see it.

Google AI Mode and AI Overview updates work to elevate links. I continue to be skeptical that this move will enrich anyone on the publishing side, but at least the additional link visibility is an ethical win that we can all get behind.

Amazon launches two Bee AI recorders to remember everything you say. Nope. Absolutely not.

Google updates Android earthquake alerts with more info, expands to 200+ regions. This is a good news story for anyone in a region commonly affected by earthquakes, and I hope it saves lives.

Gemini 4 Argon is now rolling out to Google’s Antigravity for AI Pro subscribers. Paid AI Pro subscribers. Paid. 

Google restricts every free AI Pro trial from Pixel & more compared to paid subscribers

Nest’s Halloween doorbell chimes are live now through November 1. I love these chimes and I hope one day we’ll be able to vibe-code our own.

ChatGPT gets deeper Google Chrome integration including control over tabs. I’ve been using this for a few days and it’s fantastic. Must-install if you’re a paid ChatGPT user.

Android 17 QPR2 Beta 7.1 rolling out for Pixel

Walmart’s $60 Google TV streamer might be the only good deal left in streaming. The days of cheap streamers are gone (see the new $300 Apple TV 4K), so get it while it’s hot.

Google support pages start defaulting to AI chatbots – it might be for the best. This felt inevitable.

The COROS Pace 4 is a smartwatch for running and clear reasons to buy over Wear OS. Nicholas Sutrich is our newest contributor and this is his first post! Go welcome him in the comments.

Wyze’s latest weight scale has a display you can actually see, Google Health sync. Why did it take so long for someone to figure this out?

Google TV shows off its ‘new’ features in fullscreen roundup when you turn on your TV [Gallery]

Android Auto ‘Work Account’ support would allow for easy switching in work vehicles. This is a good, albeit niche, idea.

Spotify’s ‘QR code verification’ cracks down on sharing and could ban you for a year. Yikes, that’s not particularly customer-first, is it?

It’s been a busy week for Samsung news

Samsung just released Android 17 updates for Galaxy S23 and several more devices. Android 17 is a bigger update than one might think, primarily for its improvements to stability and performance.

Samsung’s Android 18-based One UI 10 update sounds like it might be a big deal. One UI 9 is still steaming from the oven, but we’re already dreaming of ways its successor will copy iOS.

I’ve struggled to use Samsung displays for years, but the Galaxy S27 may finally fix that; here’s why

Galaxy S26 Ultra is one of the ‘best inventions of 2026’ thanks to its Privacy Display. Eh.

Galaxy S27 reportedly skips Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 due to overheating. I don’t think this rumor has legs; Samsung always goes with the best SoC available unless it’s an absolute disaster (see the Snapdragon 810 debacle), and I doubt this one is.

Qualcomm says rumors about Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 overheating are ‘inaccurate’

Samsung reportedly hasn’t finalized Galaxy S27 details, considers February launch. Wouldn’t surprise me if they’re trying to keep costs down.

Dizzying lineup of Galaxy Z Fold 9 devices leaks, including the Galaxy Z ‘Slide’. Next year’s Galaxy foldable lineup looks crowded.

Welcome to Cc:, where I ask interesting people in the community about what’s making them happy both inside and outside the world of tech. This week, I’m speaking with Ben Schoon, 9to5Google’s Senior Editor and one of the best disc golf players I know.

Who are you?

Ben Schoon

What do you do for work?

I am the Senior Editor at 9to5Google, covering daily news, reviews, and more.

What do you do for fun?

Disc golf has basically taken over my non-work life. I’ve got a 170-plus-week streak of playing at least once a week, I frequently play in and even run tournaments, and I’m absolutely hooked.

What is your relationship like with technology these days?

I still deeply enjoy tech, but the AI era has certainly changed my outlook, and not always in the best ways. On the bright side, it’s cool to see the explosion of what tech can do. On the downside, let’s just say that humanity tends to take the path of least resistance, and AI enables that in some frightening ways.

What are three apps you can’t live without and why?

Nourish has been a huge part of my weight-loss journey over the past couple of years, helping me log food more easily while also connecting with an actual nutritionist. 

UDisc might as well be in my dock row given how frequently I’m out on the disc golf course.

Beeper continues to be indispensable given my multi-device lifestyle.

What is a gadget that you love right now?

The Fitbit Air has been a refreshing bit of simplicity in a busy tech life.

How does AI fit into your life right now?

As mentioned, my relationship with AI isn’t always positive. Lately I find myself more and more frustrated by the impact it’s made on day-to-day life for everyone, and wishing we could go back. Ultimately, I barely find myself using AI in my own life, but I do appreciate those occasional bits of delight that come from finding a good use for it.

What’s a TV show you recently watched and loved?

Recently started listening to the “How We Made Your Mother” podcast and it’s unlocked a fresh rewatch of the early seasons of HIMYM with some new perspectives.

What’s a movie you recently watched and loved?

Project Hail Mary hasn’t left my mind all year. It continues to be a source of joy from its excellent visuals and plot, and the vocal stims that still find their way into daily conversation with my wife and me.

What’s a game you recently played and loved?

Star Wars: Galactic Racer has me hooked right now. I love a good racing game, and this one delivers a real challenge.

What’s something offline you do every day that brings you joy?

Spend time around my crazy doggos.

➡️ FWD:

This section has some of our favorite stuff from around the internet. Great videos, weird memes, fun reads, recommended apps, whatever. Send us your recommendations!

Over the weekend, I caught up on some podcasts and just happened to listen to an episode of The New York Times’ The Daily from a few days ago. “When A.I. Comes for Your Purpose in Life” features an interview with mathematician and Cornell University professor Steven Strogatz, and is among the most poignant and honest conversations I’ve heard about how AI stands to reconfigure everyone’s jobs — even the ones we previously considered unassailable.

There’s recently been an abundance of great reporting on how AI is changing the fields of mathematics and science. But I think some of it lacks the emotional intelligence to acknowledge that LLMs are not just disrupting jobs and preempting discovery; their seemingly infinite potential undermines what it means to be a human solving problems for their own sake. As people become increasingly comfortable offloading their cognition to machines, what happens to their relationship with their own brains?

🗑️ Trash

Anthropic recently announced that it would set aside 5% of its shares to be used for the “public good,” a vacuous claim that has shades of effective altruism. Elon Musk, who is practically single-handedly bankrolling the Republicans’ midterm election, then came out with a similar, more direct offer: “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many.”

The moves are a direct result of a growing public backlash against AI’s negative impacts on culture, on employment, and increasingly on the environment, but laundering one’s reputation with the promise of future beneficence often has the inverse effect.

title: Spotify confirms it won’t stop Family Plan sharing verification, but it’s not a ‘crackdown’
snippet: Earlier this week a new method of Spotify Family plan verification came to light and, in its latest earnings call, Spotify says that it’s not a “crackdown,” but also something that doesn’t have an “end date.” more…
fullText:
Earlier this week a new method of Spotify Family plan verification came to light and, in its latest earnings call, Spotify says that it’s not a “crackdown,” but also something that doesn’t have an “end date.”

Like virtually every family sharing subscription, Spotify requires Family Plan members to be in the same physical household, but the music streaming app has been looser in its requirements and enforcement. A new method, though, started popping up recently in the form of a verification QR code that makes it a bit more difficult for remote participants to complete verification, and also threatens to ban users from Family plans for a full year if verification isn’t completed.

Spotify’s ‘QR code verification’ cracks down on sharing and could ban you for a year

Today, Spotify’s Q3 earnings call included a question about Spotify “beginning to crack down on Family Plan subscribers that do not live in the same home.” 

Responding to this, Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström says that this is not a “crackdown,” but a “routine improvement of our verification methods,” and something that Spotify will continue to work on. “This is not something that has an end date,” he said:

	

…this is not as much a crackdown as it is actually a routine improvement of our verification methods for our Family Plan. Family Plan has existed for a long while. It has been around for, I think it is now close to 12, 13 years in Spotify history, and it makes up a pretty significant proportion of our subscriber base. As such, it is important for us to just make sure over time that we improve the verification methods that we have. There are certainly ways, over time, to find holes around it. As that happens, we figure out how to improve it over time. This is not something that has an end date. This is not an implementation that is going to complete. This is just ongoing routine.

Reading between the lines, this is saying that Spotify isn’t going to be backing down from verification methods on its Family Plan sharing. QR codes are only the latest implementation.

title: Is the Ninja MultiPot the Kitchen Appliance You Need, or Just the One You Want?
snippet: Ninja releases kitchen appliances so often that it’s hard to keep up. Here’s whether or not the new MultiPot XL is a true kitchen essential.
fullText:
When I think of kitchen brands dominating home kitchens and wishlists alike, Ninja immediately comes to mind. 

Beyond the company’s viral social media videos and massively popular product releases, like the Crispi air fryer and Creami frozen dessert maker, the brand’s popularity may also be rooted in its rapid product launches. Ninja releases products fast, and it releases a lot of them. 

In the last couple of months alone, we’ve seen the release of the Prepi, CrushBoss, NeverQuit cookware and now, the MultiPot XL. With colder weather setting in, the 12-in-1 cooker caught my eye. Theoretically, it can reduce kitchen clutter by replacing numerous other countertop appliances, but is it truly a worthy replacement for your Instant Pot, Crockpot and even the classic Dutch oven? 

		

			

With so many new releases, how do you separate want from need? We cooked numerous meals with the new MultiPot XL to see whether the shiny new appliance has what it takes to earn a place on your countertop. 

Searing, sautéing and soups 

The MultiPot XL has 12 settings: Slow cook, sear/sauté, bake, steam, sous vide, rice, pasta, mixed rice, stir fry, shallow fry, hot pot and keep warm.Corin Cesaric-Epple/CNET

The Ninja MultiPot XL has 12 functions and the option to cook in the “Megazone,” a 7.5-quart pot, or in two smaller pots, each 3.5 quarts. All of the pots are ceramic-coated. 

The first meal I cooked in it was homemade ramen, and I learned there are a few settings where the MultiPot excels, including the sear/sauté function. 

The first ingredient I sautéed was mushrooms with butter. The MultiPot quickly preheated and sauteed the mushrooms just as well as a non-stick pan on a stovetop would. When the lids are shut, the pot quickly gathers steam to help speed up the cooking process too. 

Next, I placed the chicken thighs in the already heated pot, and they took only a few minutes to cook all the way through. The best part was that the chicken developed a crust, which added extra flavor to the dish. 

I used the same function for a handful of additional ingredients, combined everything in the pot with chicken broth and then set the MultiPot to its hot pot setting until everything came to a boil.  

Because the pot was already hot, it didn’t take long to boil. When I was ready for it to stop, I turned off the appliance and lifted the pot off the hot plates so it wouldn’t overcook. Over the next couple of weeks, I continued to use the appliance for various meals, but sauté/sear and hot pot remained among my favorite functions.  

A loaded vegetable soup was one of my favorite meals I made. Corin Cesaric-Epple/CNET

It’s not a slow cooker replacement

Despite its ability to sear and sauté just as well as a non-stick pan on the stovetop, one setting was less impressive. I used the slow cooker setting to cook a small batch of beef short ribs in one half of the cooker, cooking them on low for over 8 hours. I’ve cooked this meal before in a slow cooker, and by the end of the 8 hours, the meat is usually falling apart and my whole house smells like the dish. 

With the MultiPot, though, although the meat was still fully cooked through and had a great flavor, it wasn’t fall-off-the-bone cooked. I’m not entirely sure why that is, but it made me wish I’d cooked that dish in my Crockpot instead. 

Being able to cook two things at once on different settings is a high point for the appliance. Corin Cesaric-Epple/CNET

On the other side of the MultiPot, I cooked brown rice, and it cooked just as well as on the stovetop.

In my experience, the only place where the MultiPot has a leg up on a slow cooker is the fact that you can sauté or sear directly in the MultiPot, then turn the pot to the slow cooker setting, instead of having to sear in a separate pan on the stovetop, then transfer the ingredients to a slow cooker. So, if you’re looking for convenience, the MultiPot offers it. 

I was also able to thicken up my short rib sauce directly in the pot on the sear/sauté setting instead of transferring it to the stovetop. Corin Cesaric-Epple/CNET

Who’s the Ninja MultiPot XL best for? 

If you have limited countertop space for appliances and want just one that can handle many cooking tasks, the MultiPot XL would be a great option. With 12 settings, it has more versatility than many competitors, but keep in mind that the “keep warm” function is included in the 12, and some functions won’t be used as much as others, such as sous vide. 

At $250, it’s more expensive than standard slow cookers and Instant Pots, but it could be a good option if you often cook large meals for a group. If you’re looking for a cheaper multicooker, but want to stay in the Ninja family, the 8-in-1 Ninja PossibleCooker may be a smarter buy since it’s less than half the price but still has the essential functions. However, I haven’t tested the PossibleCooker myself.

The MultiPot XL can definitely be a great choice for some, but I wouldn’t put it in the must-have category, even if the rose quartz option is one of the cutest appliance color schemes I’ve seen.

title: Block’s new voice model sounds eerily human
snippet: Block said that the voice model can run locally on a MacBook M4 Max
fullText:
Jack Dorsey’s Block released a new voice model out of the company’s research lab that runs locally and sounds strangely human with its expressions like laughs, pauses, and cries. The company said the model, called Dessa, is trained fully on human speech and a single NVIDIA GPU rack. 

Dessa is a full-duplex model, which means it can talk and listen at the same time, just like the GPT-Live model OpenAI released earlier this year. Typically, speech models are paired with a large language model for knowledge retrieval. Block said that Dessa’s knowledge stems from the conversational data it has. 

We believe voice is the most natural way to interact with intelligence, so we created Dessa, the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built. Talking with it feels like talking with a person…full of emotion, nuance, pauses, and a natural cadence. https://t.co/r0qFLdvd6c

— jack (@jack) October 23, 2026

Block said that the current models can sound unnatural and annoying because they have text in the pipeline that drives speech generation. A lot of models like ElevenLabs v4 or Fish Audio Drama 3 use voice tags to drive emotion in speech generation. Dorsey’s company claims that emotion is built into its model. It’s not clear if that emotion is being steered by some kind of tags. 

“Interacting with current voice AI can just plain suck. It turns your voice into text and throws away an incredible amount of information text alone can’t carry. The most powerful AIs in the world can’t hear how you feel. We think that’s ridiculous, leads to a worse experience, and is potentially dangerous,” the company said in a blog post. 

The company’s researchers posted multiple examples of conversations with Dessa where the agent had different voices, cadences, and emotions. For instance, in the conversation, the bot said it was tired from work, and at that point it sounded tired. 

We made the first AI model you can have a realistic conversation with that was trained entirely on speech!

Dessa is a full-duplex speech-to-speech model that you can run on consumer GPUs.

This is a GPT3 moment for speech. pic.twitter.com/XVD8sSyJn8

— Ragavan Thurairatnam (@RagavanThurair) October 23, 2026

In the example below, the bot was talking about the person making it comfortable while sounding emotional and almost breaking down. 

Another one shows a Block team member playing a game with the voice assistant. 

The company said that the model can run locally on a consumer-grade computer such as a MacBook M4 Max or better. However, there is no public access to Dessa at the moment, and Block has put out a call for safety researchers to test the model. This is likely to test out cases where a voice agent could trick people on the other end. 

Block is in the business of finance and selling its solutions to small businesses. Square already uses voice AI to handle ordering. But with its own voice model that can run on-device, it can power a lot more business and consumer experiences at a lower cost.

title: Supernatural, the best VR workout app, makes its glorious comeback today
snippet: Supernatural made a name for itself as the de facto workout app through the COVID era and beyond, and is coming back from the grave as an independent app, starting today. more…
fullText:
Supernatural made a name for itself as the de facto workout app through the COVID era and beyond, and is coming back from the grave as an independent app, starting today.

Workout trends often come and go like the wind, but a few staples hang around long enough to be properly cemented into the “this really works” category. Supernatural is one such example. The VR workout app debuted on April 23, 2020, making it the best way to get a gym-like workout in a world where all the gyms were shut down during the pandemic. Lots of people used it and continued to use it until earlier this year, when Meta closed the studio that made it.

People were devastated. The entire Supernatural community on Facebook was up in arms. But it wasn’t long until Supernatural’s founders announced that they had acquired the rights and would be returning later in 2026 as an independent company, and today is that day.

Meta Quest 3 at Amazon

AMVR FC4M magnetic face pad (you’ll thank me later) at Amazon

Supernatural Early Access is officially launching today, October 21, on Meta’s storefront. You can get a free 7-day trial by downloading the app, and then it’s $20 per month after that. An extended 14-day free trial is available to folks who sign up for the $200/year plan, which grants a $40 annual discount by paying up front.

	

If you haven’t used Supernatural before, you’re about to be very pleasantly surprised. The game features daily coach-led workouts with popular music you’ll love to work out to. Gamers move their bodies around to the beat, smashing flying obstacles with bats, ducking, kicking, and generally getting very sweaty. The whole thing takes place in incredibly realistic environments, which the Supernatural team says are getting a big visual upgrade in the new release.

Today’s early access version launches with thousands of workouts available immediately — with all the coaches you know and love — including hundreds of licensed music tracks, a brand new home environment set in Laguna Torre, a glacial lake in Argentine Patagonia, and the ability to transfer your entire workout history from the old Supernatural app to the new one. I know my colleague, Daniel Bader, will be very happy about that.

Founding members will start with a custom bat, and more rewards are dropping throughout the early access period. Additionally, household accounts can be used to share the experience with up to four people in your home, including individual profiles for each one. Make sure you get a good face pad that’s easy to clean if you do this!

As Supernatural continues to get rebuilt and gets better than ever, users can expect more workouts and music on a weekly cadence, the return of real-time workouts with friends (sign up for the beta now), a new mobile companion app (that pairs with your smartwatch), new destinations, and plenty of rewards for returning and founding members. It’s incredible, and it’s quite frankly mind-blowing to see the entire team return this way, all without the help of Meta.

Google Maps in CarPlay now lets you access Gemini when navigating for a conversational driving experience.

title: Google gives Pixel 9 another year of free Satellite SOS connectivity
snippet: Google won’t start charging for the Satellite SOS feature on its Pixel 9 series phones just yet, despite the timer having run out. more…
fullText:
Google won’t start charging for the Satellite SOS feature on its Pixel 9 series phones just yet, despite the timer having run out.

Satellite SOS was introduced on the Pixel 9 series and has been in place on every Pixel phone released in the time since. The feature grants your phone access to limited satellite connectivity in emergencies, offering a lifeline in dangerous, off-grid situations. 

But Google only promised this would be free for “the first 2 years after activation.”

A support page footnote still reads:

	

Service included at no additional charge for the first 2 years after activation of devices. Available in select countries and languages. Connection and response times vary based on location, site conditions, and other factors.

Everything you should know about Satellite SOS on Pixel 9 before you ever have to use it

As of August 2026, that timer was up for Pixel 9 series devices. Yet, Google showed no signs of charging for the feature, but it wasn’t exactly clear what would happen next. Now, the company has confirmed that, at least for another year, Satellite SOS on Pixel 9 remains free.

The company confirmed the news to PCMag, saying:

Confirming that we’ve extended this offering, at no additional cost, for one additional year. We have no details to share beyond that at this time.

So far, there have been no hints even behind the scenes of Google introducing a way to charge for Satellite SOS on Pixel phones. Apple, which introduced this functionality prior to Google, recently confirmed that it would also be extending the “free trial” of satellite connections for iPhone 14, 15, and 16, and there’s also no word on what Apple might charge for the feature.

Would you pay for Satellite SOS on your Pixel if Google starts charging for it?

title: Starlink seems to be working normally again in Ukraine
snippet: Elon Musk reportedly ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine's Starlink access.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

1:46 PM PDT · October 24, 2026

Image Credits:Jagmeet Singh / TechCrunch

		

							

											
									

					

	

SpaceX appears to have lifted restrictions the Ukrainian military’s of use Starshield — the military-grade version of the company’s Starlink internet system.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara told reporters that Starshield appears to be working normally again, although the military is still conducting tests and has not received an explanation for the restrictions.

This follows a 10-day period where Ukrainian drones would lose internet connectivity when flying at speeds of around 100 miles per hour, resulting in the military losing control of some drones, while others became more vulnerable because they were flying more slowly.

President Donald Trump reportedly called SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to restore Starshield service. Both Trump and Musk have criticized Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, with Musk recently posting, “Zelensky has gone too far.”

The WSJ previously reported that Musk ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine’s Starlink access, though some sources claimed he’d discussed it with the Trump administration first. Musk claimed in a post on X that Ukraine had “violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people.”

“Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately,” Musk said. “This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.”

title: TikTok accused of profiting from illegal child sexual exploitation videos
snippet: TikTok has been accused of profiting from illegal child sexual exploitation videos posted on its platform. The allegations were made by former and current employees, who say that the company failed to properly respond to internal reports … more…
fullText:
TikTok has been accused of profiting from illegal child sexual exploitation videos posted on its platform. The allegations were made by former and current employees, who say that the company failed to properly respond to internal reports …

NPR reports.

Employees raised the alarm about minors appearing in sexual content on the app, which viewers could pay to access and the company would profit from – a potential financial crime. They also flagged that users under 18 were using loopholes to bypass age-restricted content and to block parents and guardians from reviewing their activity on the app. TikTok also refrained from conducting surveys to assess the ages of its users because it was concerned that it would have to turn the results over to the Federal Trade Commission, the documents show.

Employees say that senior leaders were aware of the issues, but their responses were inadequate. Social media companies are required by law to report suspected CSAM, as well as suspicions regarding money being obtained illegally through their platforms.

The report additionally says concerns were expressed internally about young users being shown content related to suicide and self-harm, and that the platform was not taking proper steps to tackle this.

TikTok is one of the most popular apps on the App Store, with a high proportion of teenage users. The company responded by saying that the claims made in the story are “clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works.”

title: America, You Can’t Get This Powerhouse Phone. It’s a Shame
snippet: Oppo’s ambitious plans for the Find X10 Pro and its future high-end phones are America’s loss but Europe’s gain.
fullText:
If the only two names that pop into your head when you think about the best phones on the market are Apple and Samsung, frankly, you’re thinking too small.

Chinese phone-makers aren’t just making phones that rival those from Apple and Samsung; in some respects, they’re surpassing the iPhones and Galaxys — in batteries and fast charging, and especially when it comes to cameras.

On Wednesday, Oppo launched its latest photography-focused high-end phones, the Find X10 and Find X10 Pro, on the sun-bleached Spanish island of Mallorca. A finca covered in bougainvillea and surrounded by gnarled olive groves and roving wild goats might at first glance seem like an offbeat choice for a Chinese tech giant to stage a global launch event, but the decision is far from random. Spain is Oppo’s biggest European market, and it’s only getting bigger.

			

More from CNET

It’s a story we’re seeing repeat itself around the world. According to researchers Counterpoint and Omdia, Oppo was the fourth-largest phone-maker globally by shipments in the first half of this year. Already well established in China, the company is now seeing growth across the globe, and in Europe in particular.

It’s an impressive feat given that growing a smartphone business is harder than it’s ever been. It’s no secret that RAMageddon, the ongoing memory shortage, is pushing up phone prices and causing a massive drop in shipments. 

Phone-makers might be putting on a brave face as they release new devices to the world, but behind the scenes they’re scrambling to draw up new strategies that will hopefully see them through in both the short and long term.

Growing sales of flagship and premium phones will be key to their survival, said Runar Bjorhovde, principal analyst at market research firm Omdia, during a briefing at the Oppo event. Compared with the budget and midrange segments, the high-end segment is relatively resilient.

You might think that means more exciting (if expensive) phones everywhere – witness the launch of Apple’s folding iPhone Duo, which starts at $1,999 – particularly in wealthy countries such as the US. But that’s not exactly the case.

Bad news for US phone buyers

When it comes to premium phone markets, none is larger or more profitable than the US. And yet Oppo and other Chinese smartphone-makers are steering well clear.

There are several reasons for this. Firstly, they don’t have Apple’s and Samsung’s long-standing carrier relationships that would facilitate their phones being presented as solid options to buyers. Together with the geopolitical roadblocks affecting Chinese tech companies, this makes the US simply too tricky and precarious right now to make that investment worthwhile. 

“The barriers to enter make it almost impossible to go in and actually scale there unless you have lots of money to invest,” said Bjorhovde. Instead, the money they do have to invest is being poured into Europe. (Oppo said it will increase its investment in its European business by 30% over the next three years.)

This is bad news for Americans, who simply don’t and won’t be able to benefit from the full array of choices on offer to people in Europe and beyond, including the Find X10 Pro. In CNET’s review of the device, Editor at Large Andrew Lanxon described it as “a powerhouse phone that’s well worthy of its flagship title,” praising its cameras as the best on the market alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Xiaomi’s Leitzphone.

Oppo has nailed its camera system.Katie Collins/CNET

Of these three, only one is on sale in the US, but Europeans can take their pick.

“It definitely feels like US consumers are missing out by not having the latest and greatest smartphones from the leading Chinese manufacturers,” said Ben Wood, chief analyst at FDM CCS. It’s especially noticeable when it comes to some of the cutting-edge foldable phones from companies like Honor, Oppo and Xiaomi, he added.

Breaking the duopoly

The Apple-Samsung duopoly that dominates the American market also exists in Europe, albeit to a lesser extent. But Elvis Zhou, Oppo’s European CEO, wants to see it broken completely.

“People deserve more exciting options,” he said in a briefing with journalists. When it comes to picking a premium phone, he thinks people should have a choice between three or four brands, rather than just two.

This reflects the more diverse array of successful phone brands in China, he added. In his company’s home country, there are only a few percentage points difference between Huawei, Apple, Oppo, Vivo, Xiaomi and Honor.

Xiaomi, Honor and Vivo are all now vying with Oppo for a slice of the European pie. One sign of intensifying competition is the shrinking gap between products being launched in China and Europe, which has historically spanned months. Zhou says that’s changing — the Find X10 series launched in China only a month ago.

When it comes to choosing a premium phone, Omdia’s research shows that buyers place more importance on camera quality than do people buying budget and midrange devices, but also “softer” values, including preferred brand, perceived status and aesthetics. Oppo has nailed its camera system, but the same isn’t necessarily true of the latter values.

Zhou isn’t worried, though. Oppo is squarely targeting Gen Z with the Find X10 series (Omdia research shows that people under 35 are most likely to buy premium phones), and he thinks they’re savvy enough to look beyond ads to first-person recommendations and chatbots that will provide specs-based advice to discern which product will offer the best value.

Oppo is targeting savvy young Europeans with the Find X10 Pro.Katie Collins/CNET

“We want to focus on the young generation because … they know how to make the decision very logically – they will not make the decision only following the brand name,” he said. “Young people really care about the product itself, and they can get all the information they want from AI and from social media. It’s a good opportunity for me.”

The company has already found success using this strategy for the Find X9 series, which saw its share of the premium European market quadruple between 2025 and 2026, according to Omdia.

But while Oppo might have made headway in Europe, it might be difficult to sustain this effort over time, said Wood — especially given that all of its Chinese rivals are adopting a very similar strategy at the very same moment.

Competition might be fierce, but Oppo is ready to play the long game. “We’re very patient,” Zhou said with a wry smile. “We’re not rushing here in Europe.”

Editors’ note: Katie Collins’ travel costs were covered by Oppo. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

title: PHP-ocalypse: How two critical web bugs almost broke the internet
snippet: Two critical bugs in the PHP web programming language, used by the majority of the internet, threatened to upend the internet — and it's unlikely to be the last major software scare.
fullText:
On Wednesday, a decades-old open-source web technology called PHP almost broke the internet, thanks to two vulnerabilities that had sat dormant for years until researchers recently figured out a way to exploit them.

The bugs are dubbed PHP2Shell, officially designated as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. In simple terms, the bugs allow anyone who knows how to exploit them to break into an online system running PHP, such as a website or internet-facing server, without needing a password to access or modify its data.

As situations go, this was a pretty sizable one, forcing millions of people around the world to scramble to patch their systems before malicious hackers could abuse them.

The PHP Foundation, which maintains the PHP web software, publicly released patches on Wednesday that fixed the bugs, which when installed prevent web-facing servers from being attacked. The foundation had already given some of the biggest internet companies and web hosts that rely on PHP an early headstart on patching.

Thanks to weeks of backroom chatter and careful coordination across the industry, the world — so far — broadly avoided mass internet exploitation. From Wednesday, governments began urging citizens and companies with websites to take action to mitigate the risks on their ends. A wide range of industries shuttered their websites and pulled services offline to patch their systems. Banks, retailers, gaming sites, online stores, hospitals, and some government agencies took down their servers to prevent attacks.

But security researchers are warning that the situation isn’t over yet, and that a large number of systems around the world remain unpatched and vulnerable to hacks and data theft. 

This is also unlikely to be the last major internet software scare, with some expecting the advent of AI to rapidly uncover as-yet-undiscovered vulnerabilities that are waiting to be found and abused.

What happened?

Security researchers at Calif found two bugs in PHP, a programming language widely used around the world for building websites and web apps, both on the internet and hosted locally on company networks, like intranets and internal sites.

PHP is open-source, meaning it’s free and available to be used by anyone for almost any reason. As such, it’s become one of the most popular and broadly used web programming languages on the web today.

The two bugs were first discovered in 2024 but weren’t considered exploitable at the time, and weren’t patched. Security researchers recently found a way to exploit them, prompting them to alert the makers of the software to get them fixed. 

Calif alerted the PHP Foundation, which began a period of fixing the bugs and coordinated disclosure. The foundation did this by offering the information and patches about the security issues under a tightly guarded embargo — essentially held confidentially until a specific deadline — to give big companies an opportunity to get ahead of installing the fixes.

Why are the bugs so serious?

PHP2Shell is pretty serious because it can be abused remotely over the internet and without the victim having to click on a link or open a file. This is known as remote code execution, and it’s one of the more damaging kinds of bugs to exploit because they can grant a hacker anywhere in the world effectively full control over an affected and unpatched system.

Worse, these specific PHP bugs make it possible to break into any unpatched system on the internet without needing a password or any other credential over the internet, known as unauthenticated access. 

This would allow a malicious hacker to then plant malware on the computer, such as to steal data or simply to maintain a long-term foothold that they can return to later.

Why was 70% of the web affected?

The bugs are particularly risky because PHP is wildly popular software, in part because it’s free and relatively easy to use, but also because it’s been around for decades. Around 70% of the web-facing internet relies on PHP, though its usage has been slowly declining over the years in favor of newer, more secure programming languages.

Given its popularity, some of the world’s most popular websites are run on web software that rely on PHP, such as WordPress (which hosts TechCrunch!), as well as Drupal, Joomla, and MediaWiki, which powers online encyclopedia giant Wikipedia.

PHP is just one of many aging but functional technologies that have survived waves of the internet and generations that are now so ubiquitous, they’re akin to the glue that holds much of the internet together. Oftentimes these tools are developed by open source maintainers, who are not paid for the work that they do, and as such cannot afford third-party security reviews — but are still widely relied on by companies who do not contribute financially to the projects.

%items The Smartschool educational platform is offline, due to two critical vulnerabilities with the PHP programming language, on Wednesday 21 October 2026 in Edegem. BELGA PHOTO DIRK WAEM (Photo by DIRK WAEM / BELGA MAG / Belga / AFP via Getty Images)Image Credits:DIRK WAEM / BELGA MAG / Belga / AFP / Getty Images

Was AI used to discover the bugs?

Security researchers at Calif were credited with discovering the bugs earlier this year as part of a security audit of PHP’s code. Calif was participating in the Hack the Planet initiative by AI model maker OpenAI and cloud security giant Wiz, which subsequently verified the proof-of-concept exploits that Calif made.

In Calif’s write-up (featuring comics — it’s great, check it out), the researchers explained that AI was used in assistance with exploiting the bug, but that the bulk of the work relied on knowledge that the researchers already had, and that they knew PHP’s codebase and exploitation history well.

“No model is simply capable of unearthing ‘all bugs’ with simple prompts. At least for now,”wrote Calif.

Why were the bugs exploited ahead of disclosure?

Despite efforts to keep details of the bugs under wraps until Wednesday, it does appear that there was some PHP2Shell exploitation prior to the release of patches.

Amazon, which has enormous visibility into online threats due to its size and scale, said in a blog post that it detected exploitation of PHP2Shell about a week before the PHP patches were available, suggesting that someone, somewhere, knew how to exploit the bugs before their details were broadly available. Amazon said it wasn’t clear how the hacker learned of the vulnerabilities, but that defenders should look for evidence of exploitation as early as October 17.

There are a few theories as to what happened. Once a bug is patched, the details of the patch can become immediately apparent, especially if the code — like in PHP’s case — is open source, making it public and inspectable. Exploiting the bugs might not be easy, but knowing where the bug is and how it was fixed can allow malicious hackers to understand where to target and how to develop their exploits.

It’s possible that there was a leak or a breakdown in communication somewhere during the embargo. The open source community is enormous and controlling information in this fashion relies on good-faith. 

It’s also possible that hackers discovered the bugs ahead of time, either independently or through espionage.

The PHP Foundation blamed one company for pushing the patches live hours before the embargo period was up, which could have given some attackers a headstart if they obtained details of the patch before others. But this doesn’t account for the week-long activity detected by Amazon.

Researchers say that bugs require a lot of work to become exploitable and weaponizing the bug has been a challenge — but not impossible — which explains why we haven’t seen a scale of mass-exploitation just yet.

But as of late Friday, there are now working exploits, according Trail of Bits. 

Large parts of the internet shut down, but are returning. Did we dodge the worst of it?

It’s still early days but it’s an encouraging sign that there haven’t been any signs of mass-exploitation — but we’re not out of the danger-zone just yet.

Matthew Prince, the chief executive of network security and monitoring giant Cloudflare, which also has telemetry into a vast portion of the internet, said this week that it’s seen an exponential number of attempts to exploit the bugs following their disclosure. This gives some perspective as to how quickly malicious actors are seeking to abuse the flaws for their own gains.

PHP isn’t just found on web servers, but also used in developer tools, command line and terminal packages, and other software components used by routers, storage devices, and enterprise security devices, like firewalls and VPNs. 

We should expect to see exploitation of PHP2Shell down the line as smaller IT teams and sole developers may be slower to update. There will also be a period in which various companies that rely on and integrate PHP into their own products and software, which will also need updating.

As more devices and systems get updated, the attack surface will reduce in time. But the ripple effects of these bugs could still be felt for years to come, particularly in legacy systems that have no means to be updated.

Will this happen again?

This was one of those rare internet-stopping days I’ve seen during my time as a security reporter. In 2016, a massive botnet flooded internet registry Dyn with junk traffic causing much of the web’s top services to crawl to a halt. In 2017, North Korea used leaked U.S. government hacking tools to infect the U.K.’s health system with ransomware. And in 2024, a faulty CrowdStrike update sparked a massive global outage causing most of the world’s Windows computers to crash at once.

By all accounts with PHP2Shell, the internet escaped what could have otherwise been an extremely painful and damaging day. But it’s unlikely to be the last major incident to hit the web, and this may be the first in a trend of incidents that exploit weaknesses in legacy technology. Much of this is due to inherent flaws in aging but omnipresent software that haven’t yet been discovered, coupled with AI tools that are making it easier to find flaws.

PHP, much like other web programming languages and technologies from decades ago, are “memory unsafe,” which means they can be attacked through an entire class of vulnerabilities that can force the software to leak or spill sensitive data from the software’s memory storage. The National Security Agency says around 75% of all actively exploited vulnerabilities abuse memory-related flaws, which is to say, hackers use them a lot.

This has helped to prompt a move to using memory-safe languages, like Python, Rust, and Swift, which can’t be abused in the same way that memory vulnerabilities can be. As such, these languages make them broadly immune to a broad swath of vulnerabilities that still affect their predecessors.

But that still leaves an entire chunk of the internet running a bunch of technologies, like PHP, media and video codecs, compression libraries, and other software from decades ago — which, when they break, will have massive implications for the rest of the web.

On Wednesday, a decades-old open-source web technology called PHP almost broke the internet, thanks to two vulnerabilities that had sat dormant for years until researchers recently figured out a way to exploit them.

In simple terms, the bugs allow anyone who knows how to exploit them to break into an online system running PHP, such as a website or internet-facing server, without needing a password to access or modify its data.

title: Samsung reportedly hasn’t finalized Galaxy S27 details, considers February launch
snippet: It would be “February at the latest,” but Samsung has yet to set a launch date under pressure to finalize component details for the Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra. more…
fullText:
It would be “February at the latest,” but Samsung has yet to set a launch date under pressure to finalize component details for the Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra.

Samsung’s launch schedule has been laid on the same path for years, with minor deviations here and there. The newest Galaxy S device gets released in January or February every year, right after CES and before MWC comes around.

According to a leak by Lanzuk on Naver, Samsung has set the Galaxy S27 series launch date on the fence. The laker says that, at the latest, Samsung would be looking at a February launch, so it’s not an expansive gap between releases that we might be looking at. If Samsung settles on January, even better.

The possible push may be due to Samsung reportedly not having finalized the full component list for the Galaxy S27 series. More specifically, the Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra. The base and Plus models are essentially finished, if this leak is reliable.

	

The post credits RAMageddon for the timing adjustment. It notes “there are differing opinions regarding the composition and ratio” of the devices. Read straightforwardly, it implies Samsung hasn’t decided how much memory to inject into the two most expensive devices in this lineup.

A potential storage standard upgrade to UFS 5.0 seems to be the biggest contributor to the Galaxy S27’s undecided launch timing. LPDDR6 is also a costly addition, and incorporating UFS 5.0 on these models means they need the hardware to perform, given they both sit at a price point that seems to fluctuate from high to higher.

There’s no concrete timing, and even Samsung has yet to set the date. Still, it looks like it’s highly unlikely Samsung will make any last-minute changes as big as swapping phone models, like last year.

title: OnePlus starts rolling out stable Android 17 updates early, marking the end of OxygenOS
snippet: OnePlus is now rolling out stable Android 17 updates to OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4, marking the end of OxygenOS as these devices are just the first to transition to ColorOS. more…
fullText:
OnePlus is now rolling out stable Android 17 updates to OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4, marking the end of OxygenOS as these devices are just the first to transition to ColorOS.

OxygenOS has been OnePlus’ skin on top of Android for years. It started off as a “stock” skin with some added features, but eventually transitioned into a global-optimized version of Oppo’s ColorOS. So it wasn’t a surprise that, when OnePlus shut down most of its global operations, it was also announced that OxygenOS would go away with existing devices updating to ColorOS. 

Starting in India, ColorOS 17 based on Android 17 is rolling out to the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4. The update has been in beta for a while now, but today marks the start of the stable rollout.

OnePlus summarizes ColorOS 17, saying:

	

ColorOS 17 is here, bringing a new wave of smarter experiences, smoother interactions, and more ways to make your phone work around you… At the heart of ColorOS 17 is an idea we believe in: Flow with AI, Flow Everywhere. Technology should feel less like something you have to figure out and more like something that naturally keeps up with you. From making everyday interactions feel more fluid to turning ideas into finished work with AI, we’re bringing intelligence closer to the moments that matter, helping you move between tasks, devices, and experiences with less friction.

Originally, OnePlus’ timeline put the first updates on October 29.

Other devices confirmed to be updated include last-gen flagships and an assortment of Nord devices, but OnePlus 15 and Pad 4 are the only two for this first wave. Presumably, the update will expand to other regions in the coming days. The next wave lands on October 30 and includes OnePlus 13.

title: iOS 27.2: Three new features coming to your iPhone next week
snippet: iOS 27.2 is about to launch, arriving as the next big iPhone update—iOS 27.1 is iPhone Duo-only. Here are three new features coming next week with iOS 27.2. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 is about to launch, arriving as the next big iPhone update—iOS 27.1 is iPhone Duo-only. Here are three new features coming next week with iOS 27.2.

#1: Dual Capture for Group FaceTime

FaceTime got one of its biggest upgrades in years with iOS 27. 

On compatible iPhone models, Dual Capture lets you display both your front and rear camera views at the same time. Just tap the ‘Flip’ button and the back camera will go live while the front camera remains active.

And in iOS 27.2, the feature gets even better by adding support for Group FaceTime calls.

iOS 27 only lets you use Dual Capture in one-on-one calls, but with iOS 27.2 it’s available for Group FaceTime too.

#2: Apple Podcasts overhauls ‘Up Next’ queue

Apple Podcasts gets a key change in iOS 27.2 that I’m a big fan of.

The previous ‘Up Next’ queue at the top of the app’s Home tab is now split into two new sections:

New Episodes replaces Up Next, and contains the latest releases for shows you follow

Continue Playing is brand new, located directly below New Episodes as a hub for all in-progress shows

I’ve criticized the Up Next feature before for being cluttered and confusing, so I’m very excited to see this change. After testing it during the beta, I think it’s a huge improvement that helps users better keep track of everything they’re listening to.

#3: Apple TV app supports user profiles

Apple’s TV app is about to support user profiles on iPhone, bringing the feature over from tvOS to iOS for the first time.

When you first launch the TV app in iOS 27.2, you’ll see a new profile selection screen. You can easily disable it from ever showing up again. But if your child ever watches videos on your iPhone, you might be very glad about this new feature.

With profiles, the Apple TV app can change which content it displays and recommends based on the selected viewer. And importantly, when a child’s profile is active, they’ll only see age-appropriate series and movies from Apple. So not only does your own personal viewing queue stay uncluttered, but you also ensure your child doesn’t see something they shouldn’t.

title: Anthropic takes on ChatGPT Dots and Meta Muse with Claude Duet
snippet: Anthropic is introducing a new AI assistant that can proactively manage tasks across connected apps, keep track of emails and calendars, and continue working even when the app is closed. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Anthropic is introducing a new AI assistant that can proactively manage tasks across connected apps, keep track of emails and calendars, and continue working even when the app is closed. Here are the details.

’A proactive agent that understands what needs your attention’

Anthropic today announced Claude Duet, an always-on AI agent currently rolling out as a research preview to Pro and Max subscribers in the US, with access gradually rolling out via a waitlist.

The feature is included at no additional cost, but counts toward existing plan usage limits, including work performed in the background, which the company notes could cause users to reach those limits “sooner than with chat alone.”

Here’s Anthropic on its new proactive AI assistant:

Claude Duet is a research preview of Claude that you message the way you’d message a person. Tell it what you need, typed or spoken, and it works in the apps you’ve connected, lets you know when something needs you, and is designed to ask before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything.

The company says invitations will go out in waves and adds that “Claude Duet isn’t available on Team or Enterprise plans yet,” though it plans to expand availability to those subscriptions in the future.

We’re opening a research preview of Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent.

It comes to you with what needs your attention, completes tasks you ask of it, keeps working when you step away, and checks with you before it acts on your behalf. pic.twitter.com/kt8gAbWuX8

— Claude (@claudeai) October 21, 2026

Anthropic says that Claude Duet uses the same memories, skills, and connectors as regular Claude, and can even search past conversations so users don’t have to repeat themselves.

Claude Duet runs on its own cloud-based computer, allowing it to continue working even after users close the app.

Additionally, Claude Duet offers integrations with Stripe to check for unpaid invoices and draft payment reminders, as well as Link and Shop Pay to make purchases with user approval.

Here are a few use cases described by Anthropic:

Message it like a person. Type a message or record a voice message. Your main thread stays in one place, so Claude Duet picks up where you left off. You can also start separate channels for different topics, and they share the same memory.

Start the day with a brief. Each morning, it looks across your email and calendar, picks what most needs your attention, and can start the first steps, like drafting replies for you to review. Through the day, it sends updates on the work it’s doing and follows up on threads that have gone quiet.

Hand it larger jobs. Describe what you need, and it works out which apps to use and how much effort the job takes. Bigger results come back as files you can review and edit, such as a research brief, a financial model, a slide deck, or a dashboard. Finished work appears in the Make tab.

Add plugins. Claude Duet supports plugins, such as the small business plugin, and can suggest ones that fit your work.

Use websites without a connector. For sites that don’t have a connector, Claude Duet uses its own browser in the cloud.

According to Claude Duet’s support page, the assistant also has a dedicated Tasks tab where users can track ongoing work and see which tasks need their attention.

Claude Duet also sends updates to the main conversation when a task is completed or requires a decision. Importantly, only users can mark tasks as finished.

Anthropic says Claude Duet is powered by Claude Opus 5.5 and is available through standalone apps for iOS and Android, as well as on the web at claude.ai, for users who receive an invitation.
